To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the more the number of variables included in an explanation, the less the explanatory power of the model and (2) the less the explanatory value, the less the predictive power of the model.

(a) the symmetry between prediction and explanation does not hold in all cases, and (b) the symmetry between explanation (prediction) and prediction (explanation) holds in some cases, and not in others.

1) the symmetry between explanation (E) and prediction (P) does not hold in general; 2) the symmetry between E and P does hold in the sense that E and P can be used to describe each other, and 3) the symmetry between P and E holds only in the sense that the same information is used to describe both E and P, but not in the sense that P and E have the same meaning.
